Runtime mic sync must treat known speaker output as chirplet telemetry every block/frame, updating delay, SRO/rate-scale, phase, and confidence fields dynamically. Static sweep offsets are only initial state; low-confidence runtime chirplet observations should freeze updates rather than corrupt alignment.

Active sync probes are now an explicit optimizer responsibility: when passive chirplet telemetry leaves any source below confidence threshold, the system may emit bounded extra chirplets in masked windows, maximizing confidence gain per audible intrusion while respecting spacing and level limits.

Passive sync test using Scarlett output loopback as ground-truth content: 20s music run with normalized 4s/1s window correlation produced local Focusrite median delay 20115.5 samples/419.07 ms with 17 sample/0.35 ms MAD; PS Eye left 23848 samples/496.83 ms with 17 sample/0.35 ms MAD; Kiyo-left and PS Eye-right were noisier at about 3.9-4.2 ms MAD.
